tagline: The Gulf's high-surge island — Full Moon demand, thin transit.
summary: Koh Phangan sits about twelve nautical miles north of Koh Samui and some thirty south of Koh Tao, forming the core of the Samui Gulf triangle. Its economy swings on huge tourism surges — the monthly Full Moon Party packs Haad Rin with anywhere from ten to thirty thousand visitors — where ferry and pier capacity become the binding constraint, on top of a steady daily flow of workers and supplies across the short Samui crossing. The island leans on the same fleet of diesel catamarans that serve the wider triangle, schedule-bound and capacity-capped at exactly the peaks that matter most. A quiet, smooth, zero-wake foiling shuttle is the premium answer for resort guests, event surges and the everyday inter-island runs alike.

use_cases.title: Samui ↔ Phangan premium resort transfer
use_cases.body: An on-demand foiling link from Samui's airport jetties to Phangan's resorts that flies above the Gulf chop, collapsing the airport-plus-ferry-plus-wait chain into one smooth, near-silent hop. Guests arrive fresh instead of queued and rattled.

use_cases.title: Full Moon event-surge shuttle
use_cases.body: A high-frequency, pre-booked foiling service for the monthly Full Moon crush, when conventional ferries and the Haad Rin pier hit their limits. It turns a capacity-capped, queue-bound event transfer into a zero-wait premium lane.

use_cases.title: Inter-island staff & supply runs
use_cases.body: Reliable daily foiling runs on the short Bangrak–Thong Sala corridor keep staff and supplies moving smoothly when the ferry schedule is tight. A consistent, weather-resilient link underpins the resort economy behind the scenes.

journeys.today: Lomprayah/Seatran diesel catamaran, ~30 min on schedule, queue and board, bumpy and capacity-capped at peaks.
journeys.with_navier: An on-demand foiling hop above the Gulf chop — smooth, fast and clear of the pier queue.

journeys.today: Road transfer or a longtail around the headland, congested on event nights.
journeys.with_navier: A quick intra-island foiling hop straight to the Full Moon beach, sidestepping the road and pier crush.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Phangan's corridors are short and dense — Bangrak↔Thong Sala (~12 nm) and the intra-island Thong Sala↔Haad Rin hop (~6 nm) — sitting deep inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope with margin for high-frequency event-surge rotations, and Thong Sala is already a multi-operator pier that eases shore-charging siting.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta LR's ~2,000 nm hybrid range, with no charging-infrastructure dependency, extends the triangle to the mainland — Surat Thani, Chumphon and Donsak — and across the open Gulf without relying on island grid power for charging.

competitive_landscape: Lomprayah, Raja Ferry, Seatran Discovery on the Samui/Phangan/Tao triangle; all diesel, schedule-bound, capacity-capped at peaks.
seasonality: Peak: Dec-Mar dry season + monthly Full Moon. Monsoon Oct-Nov raises Gulf swell; range-gate to short hops.
regulatory_note: Thai cabotage; domestic passenger operations via Marine Department licensing. Foreign-flag/charter rules apply — partner-of-record likely a local operator.

sources.label: Full Moon Party 10,000-30,000 partygoers at Haad Rin

grab.super_app_fit: Grab in-app boat-transfer booking + last-mile GrabCar/GrabBike pier handoff at Bangrak and Thong Sala.
grab.wedge: Bundle event-surge transfers (Full Moon) into Grab as a premium, pre-booked, zero-wait alternative to pier queues.

transit_planning.note: Thong Sala is the inter-island hub; Haad Rin is event-driven.
